findings.highlight: The fact that you're only ever on campus in the morning…
findings.evidenceJa: 朝でないと大学いないじゃないかお前...
findings.explanation: Haruki answers that he had to come in the morning because Chiaki is never at the university otherwise. The English leaves only an unfinished noun phrase and never states the reason he came early, obscuring his direct reply to her question.
findings.japanese: 「朝でないと大学いないじゃないかお前...」
findings.todokanai: "The fact that you're only ever on campus in the morning…"

findings.highlight: merely a joke from him ended up coming true
findings.evidenceJa: 嘘から出た誠だったみたいで。
findings.explanation: Chiaki's earlier claim that Haruki had been appointed her tutor appears to have started as a lie and subsequently become true. The English instead says a joke from the professor came true, assigning the original statement to the wrong person and changing Chiaki's history of bluffing him.
findings.japanese: と言うか、嘘から出た誠だったみたいで。
findings.todokanai: Perhaps it's better to say that a lot of what initially came out as merely a joke from him ended up coming true after all.

findings.highlight: Given that I'm in charge of you now
findings.evidenceJa: 所属してんだから来て当然だろ？
findings.explanation: Haruki says Chiaki should attend the seminar because she belongs to it. The English says attendance is obvious because Haruki is now in charge of her, replacing her institutional obligation with authority arising from their new tutoring arrangement.
findings.japanese: 「所属してんだから来て当然だろ？」
findings.todokanai: "Given that I'm in charge of you now, isn't that obvious?"

findings.highlight: I was able to remember the faces of everyone within my year
findings.evidenceJa: 俺は一週間で同学年の奴ら全員に顔を覚えられ
findings.explanation: Because Chiaki dragged the new transfer around, every student in Haruki's year learned and remembered his face within a week. The English reverses that social result and says Haruki learned everyone else's faces.
findings.japanese:
けれど、こいつのこの仕打ちが原因で、
俺は一週間で同学年の奴ら全員に顔を覚えられ...
findings.todokanai: Then again, thanks to these splurges of hers, I was able to remember the faces of everyone within my year in a mere week…

findings.highlight: I wasn't joking, you know?
findings.evidenceJa: ネタにし切れてないよ？
findings.explanation: After Haruki tries to turn Chiaki's painfully accurate warning into a jab at her, she points out that he has not fully managed to make his response into a joke. The English instead says Chiaki herself was not joking, losing her observation that his attempted deflection still exposes genuine hurt.
findings.japanese: 「ネタにし切れてないよ？」
findings.todokanai: "I wasn't joking, you know?"

findings.highlight: without fear of reservation
findings.evidenceJa: 見返りが来ることを恐れずに世話を焼けることが、俺にとってはありがたかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki is grateful that he can care for Chiaki without fearing any reciprocal return—especially the stronger feelings his kindness has elicited from other women. “Without fear of reservation” is defective and fails to state what he fears coming back, obscuring the central reason this friendship feels safe.
findings.japanese:
見返りが来ることを恐れずに世話を焼けることが、
俺にとってはありがたかった。
findings.todokanai: I'm grateful to have someone whose business I can butt into without fear of reservation like this.

findings.highlight: I can't stand this girl.
findings.evidenceJa: やっぱ苦手だ、この女。
findings.explanation: After Chiaki's sexual teasing, Haruki corrects himself back to saying she is difficult for him to handle. The English says he cannot stand her, changing affectionate exasperation inside a friendship he has just called irreplaceable into outright dislike.
findings.japanese: やっぱ苦手だ、この女。
findings.todokanai: I can't stand this girl.

findings.highlight: Should I joke about how her motivation always seems to be in the wrong place, or respect her ability to calmly do these things I've never even thought of?
findings.evidenceJa:
相変わらず目の付け所がエッジと言うか、
俺が思いつかないことを平然とやってのけると言うか。
findings.explanation: Haruki describes Chiaki's edgy choice of focus and ability to do what he would never conceive; the English changes the first trait to misplaced motivation and invents a joke-versus-respect choice.
findings.japanese:
相変わらず目の付け所がエッジと言うか、
俺が思いつかないことを平然とやってのけると言うか。
findings.todokanai: Should I joke about how her motivation always seems to be in the wrong place, or respect her ability to calmly do these things I've never even thought of?

findings.highlight: Your mistress, then?
findings.evidenceJa: 春希のワケあり女？
findings.explanation: Chiaki revises “girlfriend” to a woman with some complicated or compromising connection to Haruki. The English specifies a mistress, inventing an illicit sexual relationship rather than preserving the deliberately vague suspicion.
findings.japanese: 「春希のワケあり女？」
findings.todokanai: "Your mistress, then?"

findings.highlight: "The truth is… I got into a little mess with one of her friends. She got pretty upset over it."
findings.evidenceJa:
「実は...彼女の友達に、ちょっと悪いことして。
それで彼女を怒らせてて」
findings.explanation: Haruki admits he did something a little bad to Koharu's friend; “got into a little mess with” weakens his agency and wrongdoing into a mutual situation.
findings.japanese:
「実は...彼女の友達に、ちょっと悪いことして。
それで彼女を怒らせてて」
findings.todokanai: "The truth is… I got into a little mess with one of her friends. She got pretty upset over it."

findings.highlight: you pervert! Pedophile! Criminal!
findings.evidenceJa: よっ、色男。年下殺し。犯罪者
findings.explanation: Chiaki jokingly escalates from “ladies' man” to “killer of younger girls” to “criminal” after summarizing the failed communication. The English replaces the first two teasing labels with “pervert” and “pedophile,” inventing a direct accusation of sexual deviance and child abuse that the source does not make.
findings.japanese:
「届かない想いに、伝わらない言葉に、
そして、わかってくれない大人...
よっ、色男。年下殺し。犯罪者」
findings.todokanai: "Feelings that couldn't be conveyed, words that were never said, and an adult who just wouldn't understand… Well, how's it going, you pervert! Pedophile! Criminal!"

findings.highlight: There's no way it'd go that smoothly.
findings.evidenceJa: そこまで甘える訳にいくかよ。
findings.explanation: Haruki thinks he cannot impose on or depend on Chiaki to that extent; “There's no way it'd go that smoothly” changes reluctance to accept help into doubt about success.
findings.japanese: そこまで甘える訳にいくかよ。
findings.todokanai: There's no way it'd go that smoothly.

findings.highlight: "This is the dilemma he's struggling with. Despite still holding on to his kind and caring attitude, he can't bear accepting others' gratitude."
findings.evidenceJa:
「だから、いつもジレンマを抱えてる。
人にとても優しくしてしまうのに、
人から優しくしてもらうのが耐えられない」
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot bear receiving kindness from others, but the English narrows this to accepting gratitude.
findings.japanese:
「だから、いつもジレンマを抱えてる。
人にとても優しくしてしまうのに、
人から優しくしてもらうのが耐えられない」
findings.todokanai: "This is the dilemma he's struggling with. Despite still holding on to his kind and caring attitude, he can't bear accepting others' gratitude."

findings.highlight: "No, I should be the one saying that. Because after this, you still need to go through this difficult conversation with your friend."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ううん、おあいこ。
だって、あなたもこれから、
友達に辛い話をしなくちゃならないんだから」
findings.explanation: Chiaki says she and Koharu are even because Koharu must now tell her friend something painful; “I should be the one saying that” loses the reciprocal balance.
findings.japanese:
「ううん、おあいこ。
だって、あなたもこれから、
友達に辛い話をしなくちゃならないんだから」
findings.todokanai: "No, I should be the one saying that. Because after this, you still need to go through this difficult conversation with your friend."

findings.highlight: around Nishiguchi
findings.evidenceJa: 春希のマンション、西口の方だよね？
findings.explanation: Chiaki says Haruki's apartment is on the west-exit side of the station. The English treats 西口, “west exit,” as a proper place name, “Nishiguchi,” so the direction she remembers becomes a nonexistent named location.
findings.japanese:
「さ、じゃあ行こか。
確か春希のマンション、西口の方だよね？」
findings.todokanai: "Then let's get going. Your apartment's around Nishiguchi, right, Haruki?"

findings.highlight: …Well, before all that, we should focus on whether or not she'll actually graduate.
findings.evidenceJa:
...まぁ、そもそも卒業どころか進級すら怪しいからこそ、
今ここにいる訳だけど。
findings.explanation: Chiaki may not even advance to the next year, let alone graduate; the English mentions only the more distant graduation risk.
findings.japanese:
...まぁ、そもそも卒業どころか進級すら怪しいからこそ、
今ここにいる訳だけど。
findings.todokanai: …Well, before all that, we should focus on whether or not she'll actually graduate.

findings.highlight: I might have been very dedicated.
findings.evidenceJa: あんなに練習したけれど。あんなにしごかれもしたけれど。
findings.explanation: Haruki remembers both practicing intensely and being drilled or put through severe training, preserving Kazusa's role in teaching him. The English turns the second experience into Haruki's own dedication, deleting the other person's forceful coaching from his reason the guitar still carries memories.
findings.japanese:
あんなに練習したけれど。
あんなにしごかれもしたけれど。
findings.todokanai: I might have practiced very hard. I might have been very dedicated.

findings.highlight: "I feel kind of bad if you're saying you did that because of me…"
findings.evidenceJa: 「あたしのせいにされても困るんだけどなぁ」
findings.explanation: Chiaki objects to Haruki making her his excuse for rejecting the call, while the English says she feels bad if he did it because of her.
findings.japanese: 「あたしのせいにされても困るんだけどなぁ」
findings.todokanai: "I feel kind of bad if you're saying you did that because of me…"

findings.highlight: "No, no, you can't look. The first person I have to show this to is…"
findings.evidenceJa:
「駄目、駄目、見ちゃ駄目。
だって、わたしが最初に伝えたいのは...」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she wants to be the first to tell someone the news, but the English says the first person she has to show the magazine to.
findings.japanese:
「駄目、駄目、見ちゃ駄目。
だって、わたしが最初に伝えたいのは...」
findings.todokanai: "No, no, you can't look. The first person I have to show this to is…"

findings.highlight: whether it has emotions passionately poured into it
findings.evidenceJa: 一生懸命、想いを込めずに発した言葉でも、文字通りの意味しか相手に伝わらずに済む。
findings.explanation: Haruki chooses text so that even words he works hard to produce without putting his feelings into them will communicate only their literal meaning. The English says the alternative is a message with emotions passionately poured into it, reversing his deliberate emotional suppression.
findings.japanese:
それなら、まるで当たり障りのない内容でも、
一生懸命、想いを込めずに発した言葉でも、
文字通りの意味しか相手に伝わらずに済む。
findings.todokanai: This way, regardless of whether the message is completely banal or whether it has emotions passionately poured into it, only the most literal meaning of its words will reach the recipient.

findings.highlight: I'm twisting the memories I have back from high school
findings.evidenceJa: 付属時代の思い出が様々に形を変え、今になって伝わってくる事実から逃げ。
findings.explanation: Haruki runs from high-school memories returning in various changed forms and from facts only now reaching him. The English makes Haruki actively twist those memories himself, assigning agency for their changing forms to him rather than describing what he avoids.
findings.japanese:
付属時代の思い出が様々に形を変え、
今になって伝わってくる事実から逃げ。
findings.todokanai: I'm twisting the memories I have back from high school, running away from the truth of what things have become now.
